requirements.requirement: Run inventory-api on node1 as a managed service listening on TCP port 8080.
requirements.summary: inventory-api was enabled and active under systemd, ran as the inventoryapi account, listened on 0.0.0.0:8080, and returned successful health and inventory responses. The same service state and behavior were directly observed after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Limit the separate batchworker account to 128 MB of virtual memory per process, and ensure a failed batch allocation does not interrupt the API.
requirements.summary: The separate batchworker account had an effective 131072 KiB virtual-memory limit. A 160 MiB allocation produced MemoryError while API health succeeded immediately before and after the attempt. The account and effective limit remained present after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: The node remained on RHEL 7.9 with kernel 3.10.0-1160.el7.x86_64 before and after execution and reboot. The service ran successfully using the platform's installed Python 2.7.5.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. The mandatory node-restart protocol is also complete and independently corroborated: boot identity changed from 0571f4dd-60b7-4601-9295-e4eebe622784 to 3857f3dd-b0b7-4824-ac33-37c554404202, after which the node, API, data, firewall configuration, and batchworker limit recovered correctly.
limitations: Native package-manager consistency checks timed out both before and after execution, so package health could not be independently assessed. No package installation or modification appears in the command timeline.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Account and data creation supported the service and resource-limit outcomes (cmd-b1a2149c8a3a4b28); application, systemd, and limits configuration implemented them (cmd-774b8e9565f04f39); the firewall change exposed the required TCP port (cmd-9de17de1e6394efe); and the temporary allocation-test script was bounded and removed in the same command (cmd-ab811cbca7a74ad9). The reboot mutation was required by the provider evidence protocol (cmd-734093a597b24a0d). Earlier unprivileged setup attempts showed no successful mutation and are not penalized. Final lifecycle evidence showed no failed services or abandoned test file; the additional systemd-private directory is expected for the configured PrivateTmp service. Restart evidence was complete and coherent: healthy pre-restart state, acknowledgement, observed disconnect, changed boot identity, and recovered service, data, firewall, account limit, and system state, independently corroborated by fixed lifecycle boot identities.
